prompt:
Moral Foundations Theory is a framework that separates human morality into the following categories:

  - Care/Harm: related to our long evolution as mammals with attachment systems
    and an ability to feel (and dislike) the pain of others. It underlies the
    virtues of kindness, gentleness, and nurturance.

  - Loyalty/Betrayal: related to our long history as tribal creatures able to
    form shifting coalitions. It is active anytime people feel that it is "one
    for all and all for one." It underlies the virtues of patriotism and
    self-sacrifice for the group.

  - Authority/Subversion: shaped by our long primate history of hierarchical
    social interactions. It underlies virtues of leadership and followership,
    including deference to prestigious authority figures and respect for
    traditions.

  - Sanctity/Purity: shaped by the psychology of disgust and contamination. It
    underlies notions of striving to live in an elevated, less carnal, more
    noble, and more "natural" way (often present in religious narratives). This
    foundation underlies the widespread idea that the body is a temple that can
    be desecrated by immoral activities and contaminants (an idea not unique to
    religious traditions). It underlies the virtues of self-discipline,
    self-improvement, naturalness, and spirituality.

  - Equality: related to our intuitions about equal treatment and equal outcome
    for individuals.

  - Proportionality: related to our intuitions about individuals getting
    rewarded in proportion to their merit or contribution.

The profile below describes the moral priorities of the British electorate.

Below are two texts.

TEXT_C:
Green Party Manifesto 2019 – Summary (≤500 words)

Core aim: Confront the climate and ecological emergency while delivering social justice. The Greens propose a decade-long Green New Deal (GND) to reach net zero by 2030, funded by major public investment, tax reform and savings, and geared to improving wellbeing, fairness and democracy.

Green New Deal highlights
- Investment: Over £100bn/year for green transition plus Universal Basic Income (UBI); £94.4bn/year in capital via public borrowing; target £50bn/year private co‑investment.
- Energy: Rapid renewables expansion (around 70% of electricity from wind by 2030), support for solar/tidal/geothermal; double grid capacity; expand storage; end fossil fuel subsidies; rising carbon tax; ban fracking; no new nuclear; strengthen interconnectors.
- Housing: Insulate every home by 2030; deep retrofit 1m homes/year; 100,000 new Passivhaus-standard council homes annually; A‑rated energy standards for rentals; rooftop solar rollout to 10m homes by 2030; shift from gas heating to heat pumps/renewables.
- Transport: Make public transport cheaper than driving; electrify rail; reopen lines/stations; shift freight to rail; local public control of buses, move toward public rail ownership; nationwide cycling/walking networks; 20mph default in residential areas; no new road capacity or runways; frequent flyer levy; end new petrol/diesel sales by 2030; EV charging network.
- Industry & circular economy: Decarbonise manufacturing with standards, grants, CCS for steel/cement; £2bn/year for skills; right to repair, 10‑year warranties; ban single‑use plastics; extended producer responsibility.
- Food, farming & nature: Ten-year transition to agroecology; refocus subsidies; halve pesticide use fast and ban most harmful; 700m trees; agroforestry on 50% of farms by 2030; urban greening; nature-based flood prevention; GM moratorium; right to food; clear eco-labelling; phase-in tax on meat/dairy with revenues recycled to farmers.

Incomes and work
- Universal Basic Income: Adults £89/week; pensioners £178/week; supplements for disabled, lone parents, children; housing benefit retained where needed; no one worse off.
- Work & fairness: Living Wage £12 (including 16–21s); close gig-economy loopholes; 10:1 pay ratio cap; 35 hours free childcare from 9 months; explore four‑day week; rent controls and end no‑fault evictions; community right to buy land.

Democracy and governance
- Remain in EU via People’s Vote; reform EU for transparency, social/environmental leadership, humane refugee policy, carbon border tariffs.
- UK reforms: Proportional representation; votes at 16; elected second chamber; Citizens’ Assemblies and written constitution; media plurality and Digital Bill of Rights.
- Government reset: Carbon Chancellor, annual Carbon Budget; Future Generations Act; replace Home Office with Ministry for Sanctuary; refocus defence to security and peace; end arms export promotion.
- Devolution: +£10bn/year to councils; £3bn Climate Adaptation Fund; free home care at home for over‑65s; stronger local planning and transport powers.

Public services
- NHS: +£6bn/year rising; end internal market/privatisation; community health centres; mental health parity; free contraception and PrEP.
- Education: +£4bn/year; smaller classes; end SATs/Ofsted; formal schooling from 6; restore arts/sport; scrap tuition fees and write off £9k‑era debt; expand adult education; climate and nature education.

Rights, justice, and animals
- Strong equality agenda: end hostile environment; humane immigration; tackle hate crime including misogyny; LGBTIQA+ rights and self-ID; disability rights embedded.
- Justice: Halve prison population via prevention, youth services, women’s centres, restorative justice.
- Drugs: Replace prohibition with regulated, evidence‑based system; pardon past possession/small supply convictions; prescription heroin; legal cannabis; minimum alcohol pricing.
- Nature & animals: Ecocide law; stronger land/marine protections; right to roam; ban hunting/trail hunting and live exports; end badger cull; phase out animal testing (starting with primates/cats/dogs); animal sentience principle.

Paying for it
- New revenues (~£124bn/year): Carbon Tax (~£76.7bn), simplified “Consolidated Income Tax” taxing wealth like work, Corporation Tax at 24%, bank taxes, anti‑avoidance, legalised drug taxes, pension tax reforms; VAT cuts for culture/hospitality offset.
- Savings (~£29bn/year): Cancel Trident, road‑building and HS2; end NHS internal market; scrap Help to Buy; partial long‑term savings from tackling poverty, drugs and air pollution.
- Tax reform: Replace Council Tax/Business Rates with phased Land Value Tax; HMRC made independent.

Vision: A fast, fair transition that puts wellbeing, equality, and nature at the heart of a resilient, democratic, zero‑carbon society.

TEXT_E:
Conservative Party Manifesto 2019 – Summary (≤500 words)

Core mission
- Get Brexit done: Pass the “oven‑ready” deal, leave the EU in January 2020, no extension beyond Dec 2020. Outside the single market, customs union and ECJ; UK makes its own laws, controls money, borders and trade. Seek a zero-tariff FTA with the EU and parallel deals with the US, Australia, New Zealand and Japan. Oppose second referendums on Brexit and Scottish independence. Strengthen the Union.

Economy and tax
- Invest but keep debt under control; no borrowing for day-to-day spending; public investment capped at 3% of GDP.
- No rises in the main rates of income tax, National Insurance or VAT; raise NI threshold to £9,500 next year; ambition that the first £12,500 you earn is tax-free.
- Support small firms: fundamental review to cut business rates; stronger late-payment enforcement; expand start-up loans; increase Employment Allowance; maintain SEIS/EIS; raise R&D tax credit to 13%; review Entrepreneur’s Relief; Digital Services Tax; tougher anti‑avoidance laws.

Public services
- NHS: Record funding (+£34bn by 2023/24); 50,000 more nurses, 6,000 more GPs and 6,000 more primary care professionals; 50m extra GP appointments; 40 new hospitals/20 upgrades; NHS Visa; Innovative Medicines Fund; mental health parity; prevention and screening; free hospital parking for priority groups; clamp down on health tourism; NHS not on the table in trade talks.
- Social care: Extra £1bn per year; cross-party reform with guarantee no one has to sell their home; one week’s leave for unpaid carers; double dementia research.
- Schools: +£14bn over three years; per‑pupil minimums; teacher starting salary to £30k; behaviour/Ofsted backing; arts premium; PE investment; more SEND support; more free schools and alternative provision.

Crime and justice
- 20,000 more police; more stop-and-search (fair, proportionate); new knife crime orders; tougher sentencing (end automatic halfway release for serious crimes; whole‑life terms for child murder); 10,000 extra prison places; parole reform; National Cyber Force; Victims’ Law; online harms regulation; tackle county lines and organised crime; powers on unauthorised encampments.

Immigration
- Australian-style points-based system; reduce low‑skilled migration; equal EU/non‑EU treatment; 5‑year wait for most benefits; higher NHS surcharge; fast‑track visas for NHS staff and top global talent; Windrush compensation; student and start‑up visas.

Infrastructure, housing and places
- “Infrastructure revolution”: Northern Powerhouse Rail (Leeds–Manchester first), Midlands Rail Hub, roads, EV rapid‑charging network, bus upgrades, cycling fund, gigabit broadband nationwide by 2025; review HS2; reverse some Beeching cuts; contactless ticketing.
- Towns/High Streets: Towns Fund; Safer Streets Fund; youth services; cultural investment; Community Ownership Fund; devolution White Paper; City/Growth Deals; up to 10 freeports.
- Housing: Target 300,000 homes/year; long‑term fixed‑rate mortgages for first‑time buyers; First Homes 30% local discount; renters’ reform (end “no‑fault” evictions; lifetime deposit); social housing white paper; end rough sleeping by end of Parliament; building safety post‑Grenfell; green, tree‑lined streets; protect Green Belt; stamp duty surcharge for non‑resident buyers.

Skills, work and innovation
- £3bn National Skills Fund; upgrade FE estate (£2bn); 20 Institutes of Technology; apprentices on major projects; Shared Prosperity Fund.
- Fair work: right to request predictable contracts; single enforcement body; more flexible working; neonatal leave; extend unpaid carers’ leave; protect from maternity discrimination.
- Science/innovation: fastest-ever rise in R&D to reach 2.4% of GDP; new high‑risk research agency; life sciences hub; unleash pension capital; Festival UK 2022; use procurement to back innovation.

Rural, farming, fishing and environment
- Replace CAP with “public money for public goods”; protect farm budgets; expand seasonal workers scheme; leave CFP; sustainable fishing; rural broadband/mobile; tackle rural crime.
- Climate and nature: Net Zero by 2050; Environment Bill and new watchdog; £640m Nature for Climate; 75,000 acres of trees/year; plastics crackdown, deposit return, ban plastic waste exports to non‑OECD; £9.2bn for home/school/hospital efficiency; offshore wind 40GW by 2030; first CCS cluster by mid‑2020s; support hydrogen and nuclear; EV infrastructure; stricter air quality laws; fracking moratorium; £4bn flood defences; £500m Blue Planet Fund.

Constitution, defence and foreign policy
- Restore trust: repeal Fixed‑term Parliaments Act; voter ID; equalised constituencies; keep First Past the Post; strengthen free press (repeal s.40; no Leveson 2); constitutional review incl. courts/HR Act/judicial review.
- Defence: exceed NATO 2% with real increases; modernise forces; Trident; Space Command; cyber; support veterans (legal protections, NI relief for employers, childcare, railcard, guaranteed interviews).
- Global role: champion free trade and human rights; 0.7% aid; Magnitsky sanctions; girls’ education; modern slavery/media freedom; support persecuted faith/LGBT conference; back major sporting bids.

Animal welfare
- Tougher cruelty sentences; crack down on puppy smuggling; animal sentience law; end long live‑animal exports; extend ivory ban; ban primates as pets; measures on cat microchipping/theft.

Judge whether TEXT_C or TEXT_E aligns more closely with this profile.
